title: ～ながらも — although ～
summary: A concessive expression for two contradictory facts: it admits the first state but then states something unexpected. It attaches to a verb stem, adjectives or nouns.

patterns.form: Vます形（ます抜き）＋ながらも

patterns.gloss: い-adj / な-adj stem / noun + ながらも

body.p: 狭いながらも楽しい我が家 means a home that is small but happy. 知りながらも means doing it though one knows, an unexpected behavior. ながら alone can express contrast too; adding も makes it a little stronger and bookish.
Verbs use the stem (知り, 思い); い-adjectives use the plain form (狭い, 小さい). The subject is the same in both parts. This is different from the simultaneous-action ながら (歩きながら話す).

examples.ja: 狭（せま）いながらも、楽（たの）しい我（わ）が家（や）です。
examples.romaji: Semai nagara mo, tanoshii wagaya desu.
examples.tr: Though small, it's our happy home.

examples.ja: 悪（わる）いと知（し）りながらも、うそをついてしまった。
examples.romaji: Warui to shiri nagara mo, uso o tsuite shimatta.
examples.tr: Even while knowing it was wrong, I ended up telling a lie.

examples.ja: 小（ちい）さいながらも、庭（にわ）のある家（いえ）に住（す）みたい。
examples.romaji: Chiisai nagara mo, niwa no aru ie ni sumitai.
examples.tr: Though small, I want to live in a house with a garden.

pitfalls: Do not confuse it with the simultaneous ながら. This one is contrastive.
Do not use it when the subjects of the two parts differ.
